jobs.contract: Run/Attempt identity, current owner, reciprocal parent-child links, cancellation and effect settlement remain distinct. Persist approval inputs and re-evaluate current authority before dispatch; provider sessions are external references. Boundary with the bot platform track (P13): this job owns Run and Attempt identity, the parent-child links, the Run outcome set, the rule of which Attempt is current and what a cancel names, and approval persistence. At dispatch it calls ready workflow/approval, which already runs the decision again against current context; this job does not write that check a second time. The admitted design keeps these rules. (a) The release event is durable before a dispatch is started. (b) A key is released one time: with a release record the only check is Elzoo.Approval.revalidate/3, and :already_released from release/4 is never a permission. (c) With no release record the Run restores what it has: an approval that has no evidence yet stays an open wait and is not refused; with stored evidence it calls Elzoo.Approval.release/4 with that fresh evidence, for each scope; it passes :retained only after select_retained chose an existing retained consent. (d) revalidate/3 knows nothing about dispatch: :ok is never proof that nothing was sent and never permits a send by itself. (e) When delivery/effect-intent holds a reservation for the action, the action counts as possibly sent: this job starts no new dispatch for it, its outcome comes from the reconciliation of delivery/effect-intent, and this job never makes a replacement action for it. (f) After a refusal or an error of release/4 or revalidate/3 this job starts no new dispatch; that is not a claim that no send occurs, because a task that was already scheduled can still send, and that fence is a Need of the host. (g) Each restart window ends in a defined outcome, the window with an admitted intent and no attempt included. RC-48 owns only the phase with open waits and pause and applies the Attempt rule of this job without a second definition, and RC-50 calls this job and does not repeat it.
jobs.acceptance: Restart, late child result, duplicate completion, unknown spawn/cancel outcome, parent wakeup loss, stale Attempt and restored approval bypass. Child death observed; completion requires durable evidence. Approval restart windows, as composition tests with a recording Store, a valid current context, host activation and a fake Adapter that counts sends: an approval that has no evidence yet is an open wait after a restart; a crash before the release event is durable runs release/4 again with the stored fresh evidence, for scope :once, :run and :root each, and evidence that is expired or too old by then gives a refusal; a crash after the release event is durable and before the intent is admitted runs revalidate/3 and starts a dispatch only on :ok, with one intent and one send at the end; a crash after the intent is admitted and before a dispatch ends in one dispatch or in a defined not-sent outcome, never in a stuck Run; a crash after the dispatch and before its outcome is recorded gives no second intent and no second send, also when revalidate/3 answers :ok, and the outcome is reconciled or stays unknown; in each run the Store holds the release event before the first record of the intent. With a recorded release, each of these gives a refusal and no new dispatch: the policy identity changed (:policy_changed); the current decision, action or escrow changed (:requirement_changed, :payload_changed, deny_at_release); the authority of the approver no longer covers the escrowed writes (:approver_not_authorized); the evidence is expired (:expired), too old (:evidence_too_old) or revoked (:revoked). These named reasons are the cases; 'each change of authority' is not a case. :already_released from release/4 starts no dispatch. This job makes no replacement action for an action whose outcome is unknown.

jobs.title: Durable mode of a Unit
jobs.status: superseded for runtime/durable-unit by published ELZ-117; output moved
jobs.contract: A Unit that restores its state after a restart. Inputs arrive by a step call and by one declared info-message form. Each input is appended to state/event-log first, as its own record, and the pure core/operator transition reads an input only after that append. The result (state change and pending outbox items) is appended next under the CAS of the log Writer. On start the Unit folds the log; an input record with no result record goes to the transition again. state/checkpoint only shortens replay. Pending state/outbox items are offered again to a dispatcher that the caller declares; the CAS ack is the only acknowledgement point. Input identity is kept in the folded model within a declared retention bound, so a duplicate input inside the bound is not applied twice. Past the bound the Unit cannot tell a duplicate from a new input; the Contract states that limit, and the caller keeps its own guard (the engine does: an outcome for an action that is not open is late, RC-68). An append that the Writer answers with conflict means that another Unit holds the identity: the Unit stops with a named error that this Piece owns, and applies nothing. This Piece owns the one info-message form; a sender wraps its message in that form.

On a conflict the Writer reloads and answers conflict; it stops only if that reload fails. So the durable Unit of RC-45 stops on that answer with the named error of RC-45. Shared runtime boundary: RC-45 owns exactly one business info-message form: `{:durable_unit_input, input_id, input}`. `input_id` is a caller-stable UTF-8 binary of 1..160 bytes without NUL, scoped to one durable stream; `input` is caller-owned data. The ready Writer normally reloads and returns conflict; RC-45, not the Writer or RC-46, owns the stop policy. No losing candidate state or outbox is installed or offered. jobs.title: Run lifecycle with several open waits, pause and continue
jobs.status: superseded for workflow/bot-run-lifecycle by published ELZ-124; output moved
jobs.contract: A total lifecycle decision for a Run that can wait for more than one thing at once: a model result, tool results, an approval, a person, child Runs, an outside event, an event from a run resource; plus paused. A pure step over the phase, the set of open waits and one input of RC-68. Boundary: RC-12 owns Run and Attempt identity, the parent-child links and the Run outcome set; this Piece uses that set and owns only the phase, the open waits and pause. An input of an older Attempt leaves the phase unchanged. A cancel names one Attempt. Which Attempt is current and what a cancel names is the rule of RC-12: this Piece takes it and does not define it again. Owner decision 2026-11-12: time limits continue to count during a pause, and the pause has its own time limit. The person who continues a Run can give it a new time limit in the same recorded action. The total decision still names waits for child Runs and an outside event; no RC-68 version-1 action opens them, and tests supply those waits as data. Shared RC-12 / RC-48 boundary: `workflow/run` owns Run identity, Attempt identity/currentness, reciprocal parent-child links, approval persistence and the sole terminal Run outcome set: `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `out_of_budget`, `out_of_time`. A missing outcome means nonterminal; waiting and paused are phases, not outcomes. `completed` requires a committed completion record referencing durable evidence. `failed` may carry a reason such as retries exhausted or a refused required action; those reasons do not add Run outcomes. Action `unknown`, `late`, `expired`, `refused`, `resource_lost` and `retries_exhausted` remain action classifications, not alternate Run outcomes. In particular, an unknown external effect remains separately visible even if the Run later ends cancelled, failed or out of time; Run termination never asserts no effect occurred. A Run keeps one current execution Attempt for its execution operation. A retry keeps the Run and operation identity and records a distinct Attempt ID before execution. Concurrent actions belong to that execution Attempt; an effect-intent's numbered transport attempt is a different identity and must not be used as the Run's Attempt. Only the serialized durable Run owner can replace the current execution Attempt. Restoration alone neither creates a new Attempt nor retries an action. A result names its originating Attempt; an older or unknown Attempt does not change the Run phase or settle a current wait. A cancel names exactly one execution Attempt; a stale or unknown target is unchanged, not a Run-wide cancel. An accepted current cancel suppresses new work and records cancellation without claiming that an already reserved external send was prevented. An indeterminate cancellation write stops the owner; recovery reconciles that write before further work. Terminal outcomes are immutable; duplicate completion and late evidence cannot reopen the Run. Independent effect reconciliation may retain late evidence without rewriting the Run outcome. `workflow/bot-run-lifecycle` owns only phase, open waits, pause and continue. It uses `workflow/run`'s currentness classification and outcome validation rather than implementing either again. RC-50 invokes these boundaries and owns action dispatch/routing; it stores no second approval state or second restart protocol. RC-68/ELZ-114 owns action/input/outcome shapes, not Run outcomes. Approval requests and secret filling are engine work, never new pattern action kinds. Child-Run and outside-event waits remain accepted lifecycle data, but no v1 pattern action opens them. Wake has only recorded engine-read time and bypasses mid-run-message policy. A person's answer names one ask-person action and a host-verified person; no generic completed action outcome settles that ask, and text without an open ask is a new message.
jobs.acceptance: Every (phase, input) pair has a defined result; a result for a closed wait is late (the RC-68 class); a cancel for an older Attempt changes nothing; pause stops new actions while results of open actions are still accepted; an empty budget gives paused or out of budget by declared policy; continue restores the open waits. Time limits expire during pause, including the pause's own limit; a continuation can record a replacement time limit in the same action. Child-Run and outside-event waits are supplied as data, not opened by v1 actions. Candidate Cure law: totality and late-input classification.

jobs.title: Run engine Assembly
jobs.contract: Run one pattern for one host (a Run or a room); the one durable Unit of a host comes from RC-46. The cycle: append the input (RC-45); give each RC-68 input to the pattern, a pure step of RC-68 (an engine record, such as a verdict of the host gate, is not an RC-68 input and goes only to the engine); check each action of the request for its payload schema (RC-44), an identity that is new in the Run, the host gate, budget, authority and its approval rule; perform each action by its kind (an Effect through delivery/effect-intent, local work through RC-47, a resource through RC-49); append each outcome as its own input with the action identity. The engine knows no pattern and decides nothing about the work. It does the fan-out, because core/operator gives zero or one output. Durable state: the engine keeps the pure Elzoo.Budget state as records in the durable Unit, and does not rely on Elzoo.Budget.Owner across a restart. The request charge: a Run has a cap on the outputs of its pattern step, and a Run without that cap does not start. The engine counts each output of the pattern step before it checks an action of it, whether or not the output is a valid request of workflow/pattern-step and whatever happens to its actions. The count never goes down within a Run, and it holds across a restart. The request charge is not the budget reserve of an action that the output proposes. An output is within the cap when the count that includes it is not above the cap: the cycle above and the five properties of the host gate apply to it unchanged, and each outcome of its actions is recorded, also after a later output went over the cap. An output over the cap gets nothing: the engine checks and performs no action of it, does not ask the gate for it, records no verdict, no outcome and no join for it, and makes no input for the pattern from it; the cycle above and properties four and five ask nothing for it, and a reader counts it as an output over the cap. After the first output over the cap the Run does not continue: by the exhausted-budget choice that workflow/bot-run-lifecycle takes (pause or finish) it pauses, or it ends with the Run outcome out_of_budget, which the engine commits through workflow/run, on the input that the admission fixes; an earlier rule of that Piece can end the Run first. An output of the pattern of a nested callable is counted too. For a room host the cap holds for each period, a room without that cap does not start, and an output over the cap of its period gets nothing, as above. It stores no approval state: RC-12 owns approval persistence and the release call at dispatch, and the engine calls RC-12. The engine sends the released writes of an action only through delivery/effect-intent. It records the full five-field intent identity, the canonical arguments and the binding reference of the action before it admits the intent; after a restart it uses those recorded values and never derives them again from current configuration, and it refuses an incompatible recovery. An :ok from RC-12 after a restart is not proof that nothing was sent: when the intent holds a reservation, the engine starts no new dispatch, follows the recovery of delivery/effect-intent and makes no replacement action. An intent that was admitted and has no attempt gets a defined outcome too, under the restart protocol that the admission of RC-12 fixes: the first dispatch when the approval, the host activation and the admission deadline all permit it, and a recorded not-sent outcome when the deadline passed or the schema check refused; a read-only owner stays the case named below. It appends each outcome payload that it takes from the result sink of an Adapter before it acknowledges; a crash after sink delivery and before that append is recorded as a lost-outcome input, and the action is never dispatched again. The host decides the activation of an effect-intent owner one time, when the owner starts. An owner that starts without a grant stays read-only for its whole life; the engine never grants, dispatches nothing through a read-only owner, reports it, and waits for a new owner that the host starts after reconciliation. Local work that was running at a restart gets a failed outcome from the engine at start, from its log, with a loss class in its payload (killed, timed out or unavailable, the words of delivery/aggregation), and is not started again automatically. An ask-a-person action carries a deadline: on each recorded input, a wake from the host included, the engine records the 'too old' outcome for each open ask that is past its deadline, with the recorded time of that input. The engine has no timer of its own. The engine classifies an unknown or a repeated outcome by RC-68 (late) before the join of a request and never gives a second outcome to the join. The acting principal is trusted text from the host, as domain/authorization takes it. Model output is a proposal. An unknown outcome is never retried automatically. The host gate: the host supplies one gate callable with an identity (id and version) when it constructs the engine; the callable and its identity are fixed for the life of the engine, its answer may depend on host state, and the identity does not identify that state. The engine asks the gate for each action, after the payload-schema and identity checks and before the budget reserve, the authority decision and an approval request; an action that fails its schema or identity check is never given to the gate. It gives the gate the checked action, the trusted context that the engine gives that action for authorization (the acting principal and the effect class of domain/authorization) and the tenant that the host gives for the Run. The engine uses that one host tenant as the tenant of the gate context, of the authorization proposal and of the intent identity, and never takes a tenant from an action payload. The gate gives back allow, or deny with a reason code. The gate decides only: it is local and synchronous, it performs no Effect, starts no work, holds no reservation and never changes the action, and a prompt return is a Need on the host because the engine has no timer. A raise, an exit or any other return value is a deny. This contract fixes five properties of the gate and leaves the mechanism to the admission. One: the gate call is outside the pure transition of the durable Unit and outside its offer callback, and a verdict is a committed record of the durable Unit before the engine acts on it; the engine acts on the committed verdict and never on a gate answer that is not committed. Two: each action has at most one effective verdict, the first one committed; the gate can be asked more than one time for an action before a verdict is committed, which is why the gate holds nothing, and it is not asked again after that. Three: a denied action gets exactly one action_outcome input of RC-68 with the outcome class refused and a payload of a declared schema that holds the reason code and the gate identity; it gets no budget reserve, no approval request and no intent, and the other actions of the request are not affected. Four: no stop of a process and no rejected or uncertain append leaves a request without a verdict, or a denied action without its outcome, once the Unit runs, or runs again, on a Store that accepts appends; a request with no action left after the schema and identity checks still completes. Five: a reader that uses only the read call of state/event-log can find, for each action given to the gate, the one verdict, and for each action of each request the one outcome that the engine applied, by the rules of the transition (a record counts only when its result is committed; the first verdict of an action; the first outcome that the accept of RC-68 answers applied, so not a late one and not one refused as incompatible; an action whose identity the Run already used is refused by the identity check, and its refusal never settles and is never counted for the earlier action with that identity), on a stream with no Store retention applied and skipping a staged tail that the read marks uncommitted. The absence of Store retention on a stream that is still to be read is a Need on the host. The gate never asks for an approval: an ask comes only from the policy of domain/authorization. An action that a nested callable proposes is checked by the same gate, with the trusted context that the engine gives that action for authorization. The gate has no withdraw call: a later change of host state does not reach an action that already has an allow verdict, and the gate adds no stop and changes none of the existing ones. The engine has no call after an outcome, and the outbox is the dispatch channel of the engine and is not a record.

The trusted authority context of domain/authorization has exactly proposer, effect_class, own and parent, and tenant is a field of the proposal (README, Schemas; authorization.ex), so the gate takes the tenant from the host and never from an action. The operator of runtime/durable-unit is pure and deterministic, and its inputs and state hold no funs (README, Needs); a transition returns a next state and zero or one output and cannot append an input (durable_unit.ex), and the offer callback must be prompt and nonblocking (README). So the gate call and each append that follows it are outside the transition and outside the callback (property one). The durable Unit keeps completed input identities only inside retention_count, and an evicted identity can apply again (README), so the transition itself must ignore a second verdict of an action (property two). Tenant-owned, versioned artifact references in the ready Store whose bytes live in the ready integration/object-store Piece: stage, commit, abort, put, new_version, head, get, list, versions, delete, reap and status. One Store stream artifact/<tenant>/<artifact_id> of self-contained non_state_bearing records — artifact_staged, artifact_committed and artifact_deleted each carry the full version record plus resulting state/state_at, with no inference of complete history from surviving rows — under head-revision CAS, plus a best-effort tenant index stream artifact-index/<tenant>. Content hash is SHA-256 over <<hash_format::8, bytes>>, the declared positive format stamped per record and used for verification on every get; a format change is a declared migration. Object keys are artifacts/<tenant>/<artifact_id>/v<version>/<sha256>; tenant and artifact_id are validated to a safe segment before key construction. Every operation presents caller %{tenant, principal, scopes} as consumer-vouched attribution: read paths enforce the recorded access terms and access_expires_at_unix_ms (a hash never grants access), versions filters each returned record by its own terms after the head gate, mutating operations require caller.tenant == record.tenant which the tenant-scoped stream makes structural (plus the recorded terms for delete), and cross-tenant lookup returns :not_found. Appending to an artifact with a committed head enforces that head's recorded terms and access_expires_at_unix_ms: new_version checks before staging and commit re-checks before every staging-to-committed transition, so a denied caller cannot append a head through put, new_version or manual stage+commit; with no committed head appends follow the tenant rule and the first commit establishes the face, and a caller who passes the head's terms may declare the new version's access (narrowing or widening is their declaration). Artifact and index streams require low_water == 0 and validated sequence coverage through the sampled committed Store revision; any retained prefix, missing or malformed row, inconsistent version or illegal transition fails closed as {:store_damaged, info} before object reads, uploads or Store writes. Self-contained rows and contiguous version numbers do not establish complete history after retention. stage reserves the largest encoded lifecycle payload, including the maximum valid state_at timestamp width, before upload. commit verifies object presence, stored transport checksum and size through reconcile_put before the Store write; an unknown put persists an upload: :uncertain staging record resolved by verification, never blind re-put; a Store {:conflict, _} is {:commit_failed, %{expected, observed}} and an indeterminate write is {:commit_failed, :indeterminate}. Object deletes on abort/delete/reap are best-effort with reported outcomes; every already-deleted version's bytes are deletion-attempted again under reap's cleanup result, so a refused/unknown delete is retried by the next reap; list propagates storage and damage failures as errors, never a partial page; reap is caller-driven. Creation, access-expiry and retention fields use the published created_at_unix_ms, access_expires_at_unix_ms and retain_until_unix_ms names in input, public records and persisted JSON.
